daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Democratic Party chairman Agus Harimurti Yudhoyono (AHY) delivered a wide-ranging address asserting his party's role within the Prabowo government while pledging frank acknowledgment of public hardship. AHY said Democrats are part of government but must be honest about people's difficulties, with AHY acknowledging citizens remain burdened by high prices and job scarcity. He also emphasized that power has limits and should not obstruct the people's right to choose, while asserting that TNI, Polri, intelligence, and civil servants must remain neutral in every election.

  • AHY also warned that the planned Public Service Network (PSN) must not become a source of state leakage, while stating that law must not be influenced by names, positions, or proximity to power.
  • The MPR has not yet discussed legal instruments to regulate the PPHN (Temporary Residence for Foreigners), even though there is a proposal for limited constitutional amendment.
  • Home Minister visited renovated homes in Bukit Duri and asked local governments to accelerate housing improvement, with 848 substandard dwellings slated for renovation and 120 asbestos-roofed homes scheduled for refurbishment.
  • A DPR member mocked complicated house-renovation requirements, sarcastically asking whether floors must be demolished first.
  • Deputy Chairman of the People's Consultative Assembly Ahmad Muzani stated that defending another country, let alone fighting for it, is unjustified, in reference to eight Indonesian citizens reported to be serving in the Russian military.
  • Human Rights Minister Pigai urged cassation appeals over the appeal verdicts for two TNI members involved in the acid attack on activist Andrie Yunus, with government suggesting cassation in this case.
  • The Ministry of Religious Affairs inspector general pledged no bribery or gratification in the computer-based test for 2027 hajj officials, with the ministry partnering with BKN to ensure transparent selection.
  • Vice President Jusuf Kalla highlighted unemployed graduates and proposed holistic education reforms.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo met US envoys to strengthen bilateral and regional ties at his residence in Hambalang, shortly after his return from a trip to Russia. The meeting underscored Indonesia's balancing act between major powers amid ongoing geopolitical tensions.

  • The Indonesian and Singaporean air forces reinforced bilateral defense ties through joint exercises and coordination activities.
  • Foreign Minister asserted Indonesian citizens serving as Russian soldiers remain entitled to protection as long as they retain citizenship, while the Russian Embassy dismissed allegations of eight Indonesians in its military as Ukrainian disinformation.
  • The Foreign Ministry said haze impacts are being addressed to preserve regional relations, as wildfire smoke from Kalimantan poses potential cross-border concerns.
  • The Immigration and Corrections Minister met Indonesian migrant workers detained in a Malaysian immigration depot.
  • Swedish Crown Princess Victoria praised Indonesia's interfaith harmony during her visit, with Religious Affairs Minister noting the Crown Princess was impressed by Indonesia's symbols of tolerance.

Other

Soekarno-Hatta International Airport was temporarily closed due to volcanic ash from an eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau, with operations initially halted and later extended until 09:30. The disruption affected 22,798 passengers across 209 flights, with full details of flight status published. Volcanic ash also blanketed the city of Serang, while the Bandar Lampung government began spraying roads to clear ash and activated health centers to anticipate health impacts.

  • Police named 113 suspects in wildfires that have burned 4,741 hectares, while the government deployed 53 aircraft to fight forest fires and allocated Rp5.5 billion for fire mitigation in West Kalimantan, with weather modification extended to curb fires.
  • State logistics agency Bulog poured 110,000 tons of rice into modern retail outlets due to scarce stock.
  • Indonesia set new rules for halal compliance of imported products, with the halal certification agency aiming to strengthen the halal industry ecosystem and a survey showing 83 percent of consumers use halal logos to choose products.
  • Indonesia opened the fifth batch of national vocational training to enhance workforce skills.
  • Senior Minister Luhut Binsar Pandjaitan said GovTech could slash misdirected social aid to below 10 percent.
  • Customs officials seized 101 birds from a Sri Lankan national at Soekarno-Hatta Airport, while a mother and infant orangutan were rescued from fires in West Kalimantan.
